releases.name: v0.5.3 — a declined shell request ends its turn
releases.body:
# Azure DevOps PR Review for OpenCode — 0.5.3

This release removes a known limitation of 0.5.2: with `shell: "ask"` or
`"inherit"`, a shell request of one of AZPR's sessions that a person declined
without a message left that session's turn open, and what OpenCode then did in
the session by itself could get a model request and tools. A turn now ends
where the execution that took its prompt ended, also at a step OpenCode
interrupted. The tested host stays OpenCode 2.4.2. The prompt files are those
of 0.5.2, no setting is new, and your settings and saved reviews are used as
they are.

## What changed

- **A declined shell request ends its turn at the declined step.** Declined
  without a message (OpenCode's full-screen terminal UI and its desktop app
  give none in AZPR's sessions), OpenCode interrupts that step and records
  the end of its execution as a shutdown, which leaves no marker of the turn's
  end. AZPR 0.5.2 counted a turn to the first such marker, so where something
  woke the session meanwhile (the notice of a background command that ended,
  say), AZPR let the model request and the tool calls of the execution that
  OpenCode started then through, refused the turn afterwards and tried the
  pass again in a new session. Now the declined step is the turn's end, also
  where another error came first in that step: nothing OpenCode starts in
  that session afterwards gets a model request, a retry or a tool, and the
  turn fails as interrupted (`failure=permanent`) and is not tried in a new
  session. A reviewer's first turn fails its pass, as it already did when
  nothing woke the session, and after a correction or follow-up turn the
  latest usable answer stands, where there is one, as for any turn that
  fails. Where the stage fails, its line says `terminal=interrupted` (for a
  plain decline 0.5.2 said `terminal=missing-idle`). A decline with a message
  (`opencode mini` asks for one) still lets the session go on with the
  message as the command's result.
- **A host fixture for declined requests.** `tests/host-v2-decline.mjs` runs
  four reviews on the real host with a fake model: a request declined without
  a message; one declined after a background command ended; the same where the
  declined step also ended with a finish reason OpenCode does not know, so that
  its message carries that error; and one declined with a message. It also
  holds the forms of OpenCode that AZPR tells such an end by, and runs in CI.
- **CONTRIBUTING names the fixture runs each kind of change needs.** It spoke
  of "the last two" runs where six runs of the terminal UI follow.

## Installation

```sh
opencode plugin add opencode-azure-devops-pr-review@0.5.3
```

Alternatively, install the same release from Git:

```sh
opencode plugin add 'github:WTLAIB/opencode-azure-devops-pr-review-v2#v0.5.3'
```

Add only one of them. Then open OpenCode's terminal UI and type `/pr-setup`;
the
[quickstart](https://github.com/WTLAIB/opencode-azure-devops-pr-review-v2/blob/v0.5.3/docs/QUICKSTART.md)
walks through it and shows the way without the terminal UI.

## Upgrading AZPR

For an entry that `opencode plugin add` created, add 0.5.3 and remove the
previous version only when the download succeeded. Replace `PREVIOUS_VERSION`
with the version in your `plugins` entry, such as 0.5.2:

```sh
opencode plugin add opencode-azure-devops-pr-review@0.5.3 &&
  opencode plugin remove opencode-azure-devops-pr-review@PREVIOUS_VERSION
```

Run them when no AZPR command is running. Running only the first command
leaves the previous version running. For an entry with options, change only
its `package` value. See
[upgrading](https://github.com/WTLAIB/opencode-azure-devops-pr-review-v2/blob/v0.5.3/README.md#upgrading)
for the details. Settings, the PAT file and review records remain in place,
and no setting is new or required. Coming from 0.4.x, the settings need the
update that the
[0.5.0 release notes](https://github.com/WTLAIB/opencode-azure-devops-pr-review-v2/blob/v0

releases.name: v0.5.2 — OpenCode 2.4.2 as the tested host
releases.body:
# Azure DevOps PR Review for OpenCode — 0.5.2

This release moves the tested host to OpenCode 2.4.2. OpenCode 2.4.2 was
compared with 2.4.1, the last version studied, and needs no change to how
AZPR runs a review: in the three smoke runs of the host fixtures, private
sessions were sent on 2.4.2 what they were sent on 2.4.1, request by request,
once what differs between any two runs (paths, IDs, times) is set aside. The prompt files
are those of 0.5.1, no setting is new, and your settings and saved reviews
are used as they are.

## What changed

- **`/pr-check` notes another OpenCode version instead of warning of it.** On
  an OpenCode other than the tested one, and on one that does not say its
  version, the OpenCode row is `ok` and names the tested release in a note.
  It was a WARNING, which read as if something were wrong: reviews run on an
  OpenCode V2 host that provides what AZPR needs, and what a host lacks is
  still reported where it matters (the Project boundary WARNING without the
  permission hook, a command's error or receipt that names a missing method,
  the host's plugin list; see [compatibility](https://github.com/WTLAIB/opencode-azure-devops-pr-review-v2/blob/v0.5.2/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md#compatibility)).
  A script that looked for the OpenCode WARNING should read the OpenCode
  row's note instead.
- **A turn whose prompt is gone says what is known.** OpenCode 2.4.2's
  terminal UI can take the last prompt back (Esc twice before the model
  answered), and in a reviewer's session that prompt is AZPR's. Measured on
  2.4.1 and 2.4.2 by calling the routes the terminal UI uses, in its order,
  the turn fails as interrupted. Where the prompt is gone before AZPR reads
  the session, the error now says that the prompt is not among the session's
  messages exactly once and that it may have been taken back or removed by a
  compaction; before, it named only a compaction. [Debugging](https://github.com/WTLAIB/opencode-azure-devops-pr-review-v2/blob/v0.5.2/docs/DEBUGGING.md#diagnosis-order) says how a prompt is taken back
  and what the receipt then shows. Stop a run with `/pr-stop`, not in one of
  its sessions.
- **Phone notifications.** From OpenCode 2.4.2 on, OpenCode's mobile app can
  notify a paired phone when a top-level session's run ends: "Finished" after
  a run that succeeded with a model step, "Failed" after one that failed.
  AZPR's private sessions are top-level sessions, so one review can send
  several notices, and a phone newly registered without settings gets them all.
  AZPR leaves these settings alone: set the phone to notify only when
  attention is needed (questions and permission requests), or mute the
  `[AZPR …]` sessions there. This was read from OpenCode's source; OpenCode
  accepts only its own relays as a phone's address, so no notification was
  received in a test.
- **One place names the tested release.** `TESTED_HOST_VERSION` in
  `src/host.mjs` is the release AZPR is tested with: CI installs the release
  it names, the installer's closing message and the contributor's
  instructions read it, and a test holds the README's badge and Compatibility
  row to it. Comments and documents date a host behaviour that AZPR relies on
  as "OpenCode A to the tested version", and each such behaviour was checked
  again on 2.4.2.
- OpenCode 2.4.2 offers image and video generation to a conversation as
  Code Mode tools instead of tools of their own. Private sessions are
  offered neither, as before; the host fixture now also checks every private
  request of its run for their names.

## Upgrading OpenCode

AZPR 0.5.1 runs on OpenCode 2.4.2 as well (with the OpenCode WARNING row in
`/pr-check`), and 0.5.2 on 2.4.1, so the order of the two upgrades does not
matter.

From 2.4.1, OpenCode 2.4.2 adds no database migration, so going back to
2.4.1 later needs no restored database. Stop the background service, install
2.4.2 and start the service again; use `sudo` for the global install if your
npm prefix needs it

releases.name: v0.5.1 — OpenCode 2.4.1 as the tested host, and what 2.3.1 to 2.4.1 change for AZPR
releases.body:
# Azure DevOps PR Review for OpenCode — 0.5.1

This release moves the tested host to OpenCode 2.4.1 and fixes what OpenCode
2.3.1 to 2.4.1 change for AZPR, together with defects that were there before.
The prompt files are those of 0.5.0, no setting is new, and your settings
and saved reviews are used as they are.

**If you run OpenCode 2.4.0 or 2.4.1 with AZPR 0.5.0 and use the terminal
panel, upgrade AZPR.** There, a step of the panel that was pressed and not
released can be picked by a later click somewhere else, and with **Post N
comments…** that can post comments nobody asked for (the first item below).
Until you have upgraded, do not hold the mouse button down on a step; typed
commands and the panel's keys are not affected.

## What changed

- **A release the terminal UI makes up no longer picks a step.** OpenCode
  2.4.0 and later end a mouse drag whose release they never saw (the pointer
  left the window with the button down, for instance) at the next press of
  the button, anywhere and any time later, with a release for the element
  that was pressed first. 0.5.0 took that for a click. In a fixture, with the
  step **Post 3 comments…** and the next click where the question's "Yes" row
  appears, the three comments were posted. A release now counts as a click
  only within a second of the pointer's last movement with the button down; a
  button held still is a click for any time. The rows of the sessions and
  `close` follow the same rule. A release the terminal UI makes up within
  that second is still taken for a click (see the known limitations below).
  OpenCode 2.3.x makes no such release up.
- **Local instructions stay out of private sessions.** OpenCode adds to every
  request what it collects for the conversation's directory: `AGENTS.md`
  (from 2.3.1 also `CLAUDE.md` and `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md`), the instruction
  files a configuration lists, and what MCP servers, references and skills
  say of themselves. All of it went to every reviewer, duplicate check,
  rating and comment planning session, although it describes your local
  directory and not the PR: with an instruction file of 54,000 characters,
  the system messages of a small review and its preview grew from 138,000 to
  625,000 characters. Private sessions now get AZPR's own instructions and
  OpenCode's date and environment. For `claude-agent` models, to which
  OpenCode hands its collected instructions in another way, AZPR takes them
  out of what OpenCode hands over. What the Claude Code program then reads by
  itself is its own: it has the date and the environment from Claude Code,
  and whether it reads an instruction file of the working directory by
  itself (a `CLAUDE.md`) was not tried with the real program (see the known
  limitations, also for one note of AZPR's that does not reach those models).
  Your own conversations are not touched. A reviewer can still read local files on
  purpose. Where AZPR cannot tell these parts of a request apart (another
  plugin rewrote them, or a later OpenCode builds them another way), it sends
  them as it received them, as 0.5.0 did, and the stage's debug record
  counts the request.
- **Reading a file beside a nested instruction file no longer fails the
  pass.** When a reviewer's native `read` reads a file of the local project
  in a directory that has an `AGENTS.md` of its own (from OpenCode 2.3.1 also
  a `CLAUDE.md`), OpenCode leaves that file in the session. 0.5.0 took it for
  someone else's message and failed the pass, and its retry too. Such a
  message is now kept from the model and ends no turn.
- **Rows that OpenCode's read returns whole.** A value too large for a prompt
  (a long PR description, the file list of a large PR, a large tool result)
  is handed to a model as a reference to pages, which it reads with OpenCode's
  native read. That tool cuts every line after 2,000 characters, and a row
  held up to 3,000, so a model got about two thirds of what it read. Rows now
  fit, and a saved revie

releases.name: v0.5.0 — One review pipeline: independent passes, a duplicate check and a blind rating
releases.body:
# Azure DevOps PR Review for OpenCode — 0.5.0

Every review now runs one pipeline: independent review passes, a duplicate
check and a severity rating, then comment planning as before. `/pr-review`,
`/pr-deep` and `/pr-quick` differ only in the models you list for them. The
verifier is gone, and so is the split into a functional and a risk reviewer.

This release changes how findings are produced, what reports and comments say
about them, and the layout of the settings file. **Settings of 0.4.x are not
used until you confirm an update that `/pr-setup` shows first**; read
"Upgrading from 0.4.x" below before you install.

## What changed

- **Passes instead of roles.** A mode's models are a list, and each entry is
  one pass: an independent reviewer session per shard that covers function and
  failure behaviour, reads beyond the diff, and checks each of its findings
  against the source before it answers. Passes do not see each other's work.

  ```json
  "models": {
    "review": { "reviewers": ["provider/model-a", "provider/model-a"], "rater": "" },
    "deep":   { "reviewers": [], "rater": "" },
    "quick":  { "reviewers": ["provider/model-a"], "rater": "" }
  }
  ```

  One to four entries; an entry may repeat, and entries may be different
  models. An empty list leaves `/pr-deep` or `/pr-quick` off. No mode falls
  back to another mode's models.
- **No verifier.** Nothing checks a finding after its reviewer. The runtime
  checks what it can check without judging: every field is there, the location
  exists at the reviewed commit, and the session that reports a finding read
  that file. Findings that pass are `REPORTED`; the others are `NEEDS_INFO` and
  are never commented on. Reports, receipts and posted comments say that no
  separate verification ran.
- **A duplicate check across sessions.** Where different reviewer sessions
  reported findings in one file, a session of the first reviewer model compares
  them and merges repeated reports of one defect: the same root cause and the
  same correction. The same kind of mistake at several places stays several
  findings (one comment may still cover them, as since 0.4.6). Two findings of
  one session are never merged, and a check that fails keeps every finding.
- **A severity rating, on by default.** Sessions without tools then rate the
  reported findings from their text alone, without the level their reviewer
  gave them, so that the findings of different models stand on one scale.
  `rater` is `""` (the first reviewer model rates), a model, or `false` (no
  rating: the reviewers' levels stay). The report shows the reviewer's own
  level where the rating changed it. In 0.4.x the rating ran only with a named
  rater.
- **Finding IDs are `F-1`, `F-2`, … for the whole review**, numbered by place
  and then by pass. They no longer say which reviewer found something.
- **Coverage is two numbers** when a mode has several passes: the changed
  files reviewed in at least one pass, and those reviewed in every pass. A pass
  that fails costs depth, which the second number and a warning show.
- **Comments say how the review was made.** New comments end with "Review
  method: findings checked by their reviewer against the source, no separate
  verification" and the models. Comments that are already on a pull request
  keep their line, and AZPR recognises them as its own.

Comment planning, previews, adjustments (`--exclude`, `--severity`),
automatic comments and publication work as before; the first reviewer model
plans the comments. Reviews that 0.4.x saved can still be shown, previewed and
published.

## Choosing models

- Start with one model. `/pr-setup` writes it twice for `/pr-review` (two
  passes) and once for `/pr-quick`.
- More passes find more (see the measurement below). For the findings of
  0.4.6 at a lower cost, give `/pr-review` three passes:
  `/pr-setup --review-model PROVIDER/MODEL*3`.
- With models of two vendors, one pass each found more than two or four
  passes of

releases.name: v0.4.6 — One comment for one defect at several places
releases.body:
# Azure DevOps PR Review for OpenCode — 0.4.6

One defect that a pull request makes at several places now gets one inline
comment that lists the other places, where each place had a thread of its
own. The reviewer and verifier instructions are those of 0.4.5, so a review
finds and verifies as before; the comment planner's instructions changed, and
no setting is new.

## What changed

- **One comment for one defect at several places.** A mistake repeated in a
  pull request (the same wrong call in each handler, the same stale text in
  each copy) is one finding per place, because each place needs its own
  correction. Each of them used to get an inline thread with much the same
  text. The comment planner may now write one comment for such findings, at
  the place that shows the mistake most clearly.
- **Every other place is listed under it.** AZPR adds the list itself, from
  the findings' own locations:

  ```text
  **📍 Also at** (the same defect; fix these places with it):
  - `/src/orders/refund.ts:41-44` (F-3)
  - `/src/orders/cancel.ts:18` (F-5)
  ```

  In Chinese the heading is `**📍 其他位置**`. The list is plain text: nothing
  is collapsed or linked, so its own markup holds nothing back in automatic
  publication (a file name is checked like any other text of the comment).
  Azure DevOps cannot anchor one thread at several places, which is why the
  places are written out.
- **Only for the same defect.** Findings share a comment only when they have
  the same severity (high or medium), lie on different lines of files the
  pull request changes, and the planner says they are the same mistake with
  the same correction. Places that need different corrections keep their own
  comments, and when unsure the planner keeps findings apart. The preview
  shows a shared comment with all its findings and the planner's reason
  (`Combined: …`), so with a preview you see it before anything is posted
  (automatic publication, `afterReview: publish` or `--publish` after the PR
  URL, posts such a comment like any other). A place is
  listed as its finding states it, so only a finding whose lines the file
  has at the reviewed commit can be one of several places, and the comment's
  anchor must touch the lines of exactly one of its findings.
- **The review keeps every finding.** It still has one finding per place.
  Each keeps its row in the summary index and its ID, and you can leave one
  out or change its severity after a preview like any finding; the next
  preview then lists the places that are left.
- **One more planner stage on larger reviews.** Which findings may be such
  repeats is settled before the planning pages are made, and only when at
  least two high or medium findings of one severity lie at different places.
  When all findings fit one page (at most four, within a page's text), no
  session is added: that page is offered those findings. Otherwise, where
  two of them fit one page together, a grouping pass runs first: one more
  stage of the comment planner's model, usually one request, whose input is
  those findings and which says which are one mistake at several places. If
  it fails, a progress notice says so and the comments are planned one per
  place, as before.
- **"Already there" is exact.** Every inline comment ends with a hidden
  marker made of its file and the lines it quotes, and publication skips a
  comment whose marker the pull request already has. A shared comment's
  marker is also made of the other places it lists, so it is skipped only
  when this very comment, with every place, is there. The markers of
  comments for one place are unchanged, and so is publication.
- **No second thread on the same lines.** A shared comment and a comment for
  one place (a thread per place that an earlier version posted, say) do not
  find each other, so one would be posted next to the other. When planning,
  such a comment is sent back, and the planner is asked to put it at another
  place or to skip the finding a
